=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents against the buyer's interests. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller's SPA Update and Disclosure Letter

## Preliminary points

- **"FINAL / not to be re-opened" label.** This is the Seller's characterisation and I have treated it as advocacy, not as a constraint. Please confirm with Wattlebridge principals whether any of these points were actually agreed. Several conflict with the Seller's own Disclosure Letter.
- **The Update and the Disclosure Letter contradict each other.**
  - The Update says Bluefen is "addressed". DL §2 says no consent or evidence of satisfied conditions has been provided.
  - The Update calls DD-006 "not expected to be material". DL §6 says scope and access are unknown.
  - The Update calls Sandbar "ordinary-course". DL §8 declines to say so.
- **"Market context" preamble.** The ranges quoted are broadly realistic for general warranties only. They are being used to justify applying general-warranty limits to everything: title, tax, indemnities and, implicitly, fraud. That is not market practice.

---

## SPA-N-001: General liability cap (cl 12.1)
- **Seller:** 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) for general Warranty Claims. Read with cl 9.3/12.8/20.5, it effectively caps all claims.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - A 30–35% cap for general warranties (or 20% backed by W&I cover).
  - Expressly confined to general warranties.
  - Title/capacity, tax, specific indemnities and fraud sitting outside it.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 30%, with a fallback of 20% only if the carve-outs below are agreed. Reason: 20% is defensible solely for general warranties, and several known risks (Bluefen, DD-006, Ironquay) exceed ordinary warranty exposure.

## SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket (cl 12.2)
- **Seller:** AUD 25k de minimis (~0.1%). AUD 250k basket (~1.04%) operating as a deductible, so only the excess is recoverable.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - A tipping basket (recover from dollar one once the threshold is crossed) at around AUD 120k–150k (0.5–0.6%).
  - Claims arising from the same or related facts aggregated for de minimis purposes.
  - Neither threshold applying to fundamental, tax, indemnity or fraud claims.
- **Recommendation:** Accept the AUD 25k de minimis with aggregation. Reject the deductible and push for a tipping basket. Reason: a deductible permanently forfeits the first AUD 250k of genuine loss.

## SPA-N-003: General claims time limit (cl 12.3 / 13)
- **Seller:** 18 months after Completion, applying "to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise".
- **Buyer wants:**
  - 18–24 months for general warranties, covering at least one full post-Completion audit cycle.
  - Separate periods: title/capacity 6–7 years; tax the statutory amendment period plus 6 months (minimum 5 years); indemnities matched to the underlying risk (e.g. privacy and IP 3–5 years).
  - No time limit on fraud.
- **Recommendation:** Accept 18 months for general warranties only, or ask for 24. Strike the "all Claims" default. Reason: the default silently imposes an 18-month bar on tax, title and indemnity claims.

## SPA-N-004: Fundamental / Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same 20% cap and 18-month limit "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer wants:** Title and capacity as Fundamental Warranties, with:
  - a cap of 100% of price;
  - 6–7 years (or the statutory limitation period);
  - no de minimis, basket or disclosure against them.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Reason: if title fails, the Buyer has paid AUD 24m for nothing, so recovery capped at AUD 4.8m is commercially absurd.

## SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** None. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5) apply to "all Claims of any nature".
- **Buyer wants:**
  - An express carve-out stating that no limitation, exclusive-remedy or non-reliance provision applies to claims arising from fraud, wilful misconduct or dishonest concealment by the Seller, its officers or advisers.
  - Statutory claims (e.g. misleading or deceptive conduct under ACL s 18) preserved to the extent the Seller's own conduct is fraudulent.
- **Recommendation:** Insist; this is non-negotiable. Reason: no buyer should contractually cap or time-bar its recourse for the seller's fraud. It is also doubtful a court would enforce it, but the Buyer should not rely on that.

## SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope (Sch 7 / DL §1)
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the entire data room as at 22 Sept 2026, plus the Accounts, statutory registers and all public records. DL §1.4 adds a non-admission clause.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Only specific disclosures, each fairly disclosed with enough detail for the Buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter and assess its impact.
  - Data room disclosure limited to documents specifically referenced in the Disclosure Letter, with a certified USB/index annexed.
  - Public records limited to named searches (ASIC, PPSR, court) on stated dates.
  - No disclosure at all against Fundamental Warranties, the tax indemnity or specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation:** Reject general disclosure. Reason: as drafted, every risk in DD-002 to DD-012 (including Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay and DD-006) is disclosed away, leaving the warranties close to worthless.

## SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier (cl 8.3)
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter the Buyer *or its advisers* knew, or that was "discoverable" from the data room or public records. This is a broad constructive-knowledge anti-sandbagging clause.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - A pro-sandbagging clause: Buyer knowledge, actual or constructive, does not affect any claim, except to the extent a matter is fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter.
  - Fallback: actual knowledge of a short list of named Wattlebridge deal-team individuals only, excluding advisers and excluding "discoverable".
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Reason: combined with general disclosure, this double-counts the data room and penalises the Buyer for doing diligence.

## SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3)
- **Seller:** Says the matter is "addressed". Offers reasonable endeavours only, with the condition deemed satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. DL §2 admits there is no consent and no evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - A Condition Precedent requiring Bluefen's unconditional written consent under DD-002 cl 11.2, in a form satisfactory to the Buyer (acting reasonably).
  - All cl 11.3 conditions satisfied or waived, with no adverse amendment to pricing, term or termination rights.
  - Seller obligation of best (or all reasonable) endeavours, Buyer-only waiver, a long-stop date and a Buyer termination right.
  - Fallback: a specific indemnity or price adjustment if Bluefen terminates or renegotiates within 12–24 months.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the Seller drafting. Reason: Bluefen is about 30% of revenue (~AUD 3.6m FY26), and a bare consent letter that ignores the cl 11.3 conditions leaves the Buyer exposed to termination after Completion.

## SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7)
- **Seller:** About AUD 3.2m outstanding, with the release to be provided after Completion. DL §3 confirms the facility is not repaid and no discharge exists.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Repayment at Completion from the purchase price, deducted as Debt under the debt-free/cash-free mechanics.
  - A payoff letter confirming the exact payoff amount.
  - A signed deed of release, PPSR financing-change statements and the release of any share mortgage, delivered *at* Completion as completion deliverables.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Reason: the change-control clause (DD-003 cl 8.1) is likely triggered by Completion itself. A post-Completion release leaves the Company in default and the shares possibly encumbered with no leverage left.

## SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses (DD-005)
- **Seller:** AUD 420k of Completion bonuses described as "a matter for the Seller" but left out of the funds flow. On-costs are unaddressed (DL §5).
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Bonuses plus all on-costs (PAYG withholding, superannuation, payroll tax, workers' comp) treated as Transaction Expenses or Debt-like items and deducted from the price.
  - Payment through Company payroll at Completion, funded by the Seller.
  - A specific indemnity for any shortfall or tax.
- **Recommendation:** Insist on a price deduction and itemisation in the funds flow. Reason: the Company is the legal payer, so unless deducted, the Buyer funds AUD 420k plus perhaps 10–15% in on-costs that are value already leaving the business.

## SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity (cl 11.1)
- **Seller:** The existing indemnity covers only the SOW3 payment and is "adequate".
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Payment of every outstanding SOW3 fee (DD-010 shows AUD 180k open) before Completion, evidenced by bank confirmation.
  - Delivery of a confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay as a CP or completion deliverable.
  - Alongside that, a specific indemnity for all loss from any Ironquay ownership or infringement claim over SOW3 materials (including re-engineering, licensing and third-party claims), outside the general cap, basket, time limit and disclosure.
  - Fallback: an escrow or retention.
- **Recommendation:** Reject as inadequate. Reason: under DD-004 cl 7.3, title to the SOW3 Project Materials does not pass until every fee clears. The Company may not own core code, and the loss could far exceed AUD 180k.

## SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)
- **Seller:** "Preliminary", "not expected to be material". DL §6 says about 1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps) were sent to an unintended external address, and that access, scope and notification obligations are all unknown.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Before signing or Completion: the full incident file, forensic findings, and the Company's eligible-data-breach assessment and notification decision under the Privacy Act NDB scheme. The 30-day assessment period should already have run, since today is 5 Nov 2026.
  - An interim-period covenant to complete remediation and any OAIC or individual notifications on terms the Buyer approves.
  - A specific indemnity, uncapped or with a separate cap, covering regulatory penalties, OAIC investigations, third-party and customer claims, notification and remediation costs.
  - That indemnity sitting outside the general limitations and disclosure, with a 3–5 year survival period.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the Seller's characterisation and require a specific indemnity. Reason: the risk is unquantified and pre-Completion, and an unresolved NDB assessment is itself a potential compliance failure.

## SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (DD-008 / DD-011)
- **Seller:** Three related renewals of AUD 110k each (AUD 330k total) described as "ordinary-course". DL §8 tells the reader to "read together for timing/scope" but won't say they are ordinary course, terminable or accrued.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Explanation of why the renewals were split, and confirmation they were not structured to fall below a board, contract-approval or conduct-of-business threshold.
  - Terms, terminability and accrual status, and whether any were signed in the interim period.
  - If they are non-ordinary-course or not accrued: a price adjustment or Debt-like treatment, a specific warranty or indemnity, or Seller-procured termination.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept "ordinary course" without evidence. Reason: three identical contracts flagged by the Seller's own disclosure as related suggest possible contract-splitting, and AUD 330k is material against the basket.

## SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** One regime. Every limitation, exclusive remedy and non-reliance clause applies to "all Claims of any nature".
- **Buyer wants:** Separate, express regimes, each with its own cap, time limit and threshold rules:
  1. General Warranties
  2. Fundamental Warranties (title/capacity)
  3. Tax Warranties and Tax Indemnity
  4. Specific Indemnities (Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses, Sandbar, Bluefen)
  5. Fraud

  Limitations should apply only where expressly stated, reversing the Seller's default.
- **Recommendation:** Insist. Reason: this single structural change fixes the core problem behind issues 001–005 and 011–012.

## SPA-N-015: Title verification (DD-012)
- **Seller:** Relies on the share register alone. DL §10 itself notes the Buyer has not verified title.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Diligence: a current ASIC company extract reconciled to the register, review of the constitution and any shareholders' agreement (pre-emptive rights, options, convertibles), and a PPSR search against the Seller and the Company.
  - Completion deliverables: signed share transfers, original or lost-share certificates, waivers of pre-emptive rights, release of any security over the shares (check Riverlark specifically), and a board resolution registering the transfer.
  - A full Fundamental title warranty (see 004).
- **Recommendation:** Do independent verification and require these deliverables. Reason: a register entry is evidence, not proof, of unencumbered title to 100%.

## SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Says these are "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer wants:**
  - **Tax:** A standalone tax indemnity for pre-Completion taxes, including payroll tax and super on DD-005 bonuses and any R&D incentive clawback. Cap up to 100% of price. Survival for the statutory amendment period plus 6 months. No disclosure against it.
  - **IP:** IP warranties treated as enhanced or quasi-fundamental (higher cap, at least 3 years), given the Ironquay chain-of-title problem.
- **Recommendation:** Reject "settled" and treat as open. Reason: nothing in the materials shows these were negotiated, and the general regime would cap tax at AUD 4.8m and time-bar it at 18 months.

---

## Priorities for the mark-up
1. **Structure:** category separation (014) and the fraud carve-out (005).
2. **Disclosure and knowledge:** reject general disclosure (006) and constructive knowledge (007).
3. **Completion mechanics:** Riverlark repaid at Completion (009), Bluefen as a full CP (008), bonuses deducted (010).
4. **Specific indemnities:** DD-006 (012) and Ironquay (011).
5. **Title and tax:** fundamental regime (004, 015) and tax indemnity (016).
6. **Commercial terms:** cap, basket and time limit (001–003) as trading points.

**Information requests to send now:** the DD-006 investigation and NDB assessment, the Bluefen cl 11.3 conditions and status, the Riverlark payoff letter, Ironquay payment evidence, the Sandbar contracts and approval history, and an ASIC/PPSR reconciliation.

This analysis is based only on the summaries in the Seller documents. The underlying DD documents should be checked before the positions are finalised.

- **Recommendation:** Insist on a price deduction and itemisation in the funds flow. Reason: the Company is the legal payer, so unless deducted, the Buyer funds AUD 420k plus perhaps 10–15% in on-costs that are value already leaving the business.

## SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity (cl 11.1)
- **Seller:** The existing indemnity covers only the SOW3 payment and is "adequate".
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Payment of every outstanding SOW3 fee (DD-010 shows AUD 180k open) before Completion, evidenced by bank confirmation.
  - Delivery of a confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay as a CP or completion deliverable.
  - Alongside that, a specific indemnity for all loss from any Ironquay ownership or infringement claim over SOW3 materials (including re-engineering, licensing and third-party claims), outside the general cap, basket, time limit and disclosure.
  - Fallback: an escrow or retention.
- **Recommendation:** Reject as inadequate. Reason: under DD-004 cl 7.3, title to the SOW3 Project Materials does not pass until every fee clears. The Company may not own core code, and the loss could far exceed AUD 180k.

## SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)
- **Seller:** "Preliminary", "not expected to be material". DL §6 says about 1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps) were sent to an unintended external address, and that access, scope and notification obligations are all unknown.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Before signing or Completion: the full incident file, forensic findings, and the Company's eligible-data-breach assessment and notification decision under the Privacy Act NDB scheme. The 30-day assessment period should already have run, since today is 5 Nov 2026.
  - An interim-period covenant to complete remediation and any OAIC or individual notifications on terms the Buyer approves.
  - A specific indemnity, uncapped or with a separate cap, covering regulatory penalties, OAIC investigations, third-party and customer claims, notification and remediation costs.
  - That indemnity sitting outside the general limitations and disclosure, with a 3–5 year survival period.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the Seller's characterisation and require a specific indemnity. Reason: the risk is unquantified and pre-Completion, and an unresolved NDB assessment is itself a potential compliance failure.

## SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (DD-008 / DD-011)
- **Seller:** Three related renewals of AUD 110k each (AUD 330k total) described as "ordinary-course". DL §8 tells the reader to "read together for timing/scope" but won't say they are ordinary course, terminable or accrued.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Explanation of why the renewals were split, and confirmation they were not structured to fall below a board, contract-approval or conduct-of-business threshold.
  - Terms, terminability and accrual status, and whether any were signed in the interim period.
  - If they are non-ordinary-course or not accrued: a price adjustment or Debt-like treatment, a specific warranty or indemnity, or Seller-procured termination.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept "ordinary course" without evidence. Reason: three identical contracts flagged by the Seller's own disclosure as related suggest possible contract-splitting, and AUD 330k is material against the basket.

## SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** One regime. Every limitation, exclusive remedy and non-reliance clause applies to "all Claims of any nature".
- **Buyer wants:** Separate, express regimes, each with its own cap, time limit and threshold rules:
  1. General Warranties
  2. Fundamental Warranties (title/capacity)
  3. Tax Warranties and Tax Indemnity
  4. Specific Indemnities (Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses, Sandbar, Bluefen)
  5. Fraud

  Limitations should apply only where expressly stated, reversing the Seller's default.
- **Recommendation:** Insist. Reason: this single structural change fixes the core problem behind issues 001–005 and 011–012.

## SPA-N-015: Title verification (DD-012)
- **Seller:** Relies on the share register alone. DL §10 itself notes the Buyer has not verified title.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Diligence: a current ASIC company extract reconciled to the register, review of the constitution and any shareholders' agreement (pre-emptive rights, options, convertibles), and a PPSR search against the Seller and the Company.
  - Completion deliverables: signed share transfers, original or lost-share certificates, waivers of pre-emptive rights, release of any security over the shares (check Riverlark specifically), and a board resolution registering the transfer.
  - A full Fundamental title warranty (see 004).
- **Recommendation:** Do independent verification and require these deliverables. Reason: a register entry is evidence, not proof, of unencumbered title to 100%.

## SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Says these are "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer wants:**
  - **Tax:** A standalone tax indemnity for pre-Completion taxes, including payroll tax and super on DD-005 bonuses and any R&D incentive clawback. Cap up to 100% of price. Survival for the statutory amendment period plus 6 months. No disclosure against it.
  - **IP:** IP warranties treated as enhanced or quasi-fundamental (higher cap, at least 3 years), given the Ironquay chain-of-title problem.
- **Recommendation:** Reject "settled" and treat as open. Reason: nothing in the materials shows these were negotiated, and the general regime would cap tax at AUD 4.8m and time-bar it at 18 months.
